home.title: HOME · Puerto Rico Strategy Simulator
home.hero: Let the computer play Puerto Rico ten thousand times for you 🏝️
home.lead: Want to know whether “all-in corn” or “harbor first” wins more often? Put different styles at the same table, play tens of thousands of games in seconds, and see who comes out ahead and how.
home.note: This is not a game you can play: there is no player interface, only strategies playing each other.
home.steps_sub: No programming needed, three clicks to an answer
home.s1_text: Pick 3 or 4 players, put a style on every seat and press “Start simulation”.
home.s2_text: Win rates, average scores, where the points come from and which buildings were bought, on one page.
home.s3_text: Pick a game and replay it step by step; or change parameters or opponents and compare again.
home.more_sub: Five tools that turn “feels strong” into “proven by numbers”
home.c.overview: Ranks the combined results of several tables and shows who beats whom.
home.c.compare: Did the new parameters make it stronger? A and B side by side settle it.
home.c.replay: Watch every step of any game again.
home.c.sweep: Turn one knob only and find the best setting.
home.c.config: Edit the JSON and hand it to the command line for many more games.
home.roster_sub: Pick one you believe in and let it prove itself at the table
home.tips_sub: Five things so the numbers do not fool you
home.t1: The gap must exceed the error bar
home.t1_text: The error bar beside a win rate is a 95% confidence interval; if two strategies differ by less than it, do not rush to say which is stronger.
home.t2_text: Where you sit and who sits next to you change win rates. The default “random” is fair enough; for absolute fairness choose “fully balanced” (use a multiple of 6 or 24 games). Do not compare strategies with “rotate” or “fixed”.
home.t3_text: Styles counter each other, and the ranking differs between 3 and 4 players; there is no permanent number one.
home.t4_text: The same config with the same main seed gives exactly the same result every time.
home.t5_text: It thinks hundreds of times at every step, so it suits a few hundred games; hand-written styles play ten thousand games in seconds.
home.f.configs: tournaments: match configs; sweeps: tuning configs; mcts: MCTS experiment configs.
home.f.docs: docs/strategy-analysis.md: analysis of every style; rules.md: the game rules (the only authority).
home.pitch.corn-to-premium: Corn first, then switch to tobacco/coffee for coins.
home.pitch.corn-monopoly: Hogs corn, hoards it and neither sells nor ships.
home.pitch.corn-monopoly-tiles: Only grabs corn plantations, ships goods as usual.
home.pitch.corn-monopoly-hoard: Does not grab land, but hoards corn forever.
home.pitch.harbor-rush: Builds the Harbor first, then +1 point on every shipment.
home.pitch.wharf-rush: Saves for the Wharf and throws a whole pile of goods on the private ship at once.
home.pitch.wharf-premium: Sells premium goods first, then buys the Wharf.
home.pitch.build-first: All coins into buildings, chasing the end-game bonus of large buildings.
home.pitch.cheap-engine: Buys cheap buildings early, ships small amounts often.
home.pitch.mcts: Simulates hundreds of times before every move.
home.pitch.random: Picks completely at random, to confirm the others really beat random play.
home.pitch.guided-random: Random with preferences: likes shipping and building.
strat.corn-shipper.title: Corn shipper
strat.corn-shipper.summary: Grows lots of corn and ships corn every time for victory points; buys only a few useful buildings.
strat.corn-shipper.rule.0: Takes corn plantations first (corn needs no production building and scores when shipped).
strat.corn-shipper.rule.1: Buys only a few useful buildings: Hacienda (usually round 1), warehouses, Hospice, Construction Hut, then Harbor and Wharf as coins allow; anything valued below buildThreshold is not bought.
strat.corn-shipper.rule.2: Ships as much corn as possible when choosing Captain; staffs corn plantations first.
strat.corn-shipper.rule.3: Everything else uses the shared basic scoring rules (see HeuristicStrategy).
strat.corn-shipper.p.0.name: buildThreshold
strat.corn-shipper.p.0.meaning: In the build phase a building's “value” must reach this number before it is bought (it also affects whether Builder is chosen). Too low buys a pile of useless buildings, too high buys almost nothing; every style is sensitive to it.
strat.corn-shipper.p.0.range: 3–4.5 are almost the same; 5.5 and above lower the win rate a lot
strat.corn-to-premium.title: Corn to tobacco/coffee
strat.corn-to-premium.summary: Plays corn early, switches to tobacco or coffee in the middle game, builds the matching production building and sells to the trading house for coins.
strat.corn-to-premium.rule.0: Early behaviour is the same as the corn shipper.
strat.corn-to-premium.rule.1: The middle game starts when the round reaches switchRound or the corn plantations reach cornTarget (whichever comes first).
strat.corn-to-premium.rule.2: In the middle game picks whichever of tobacco and coffee is “easier to get” (existing production buildings, existing plantations, face-up plantations), builds its production building, staffs it and sells the goods to the trading house.
strat.corn-to-premium.rule.3: Still ships corn; the Trader role's value is multiplied by traderWeight.
strat.corn-to-premium.p.0.name: switchRound
strat.corn-to-premium.p.0.meaning: From which round the middle game starts (switching to tobacco/coffee).
strat.corn-to-premium.p.1.name: cornTarget
strat.corn-to-premium.p.1.meaning: How many corn plantations start the middle game.
strat.corn-to-premium.p.2.name: traderWeight
strat.corn-to-premium.p.2.meaning: Value multiplier for choosing the Trader role in the middle game.
strat.corn-to-premium.p.2.range: 1–1.5 is better; 0.5 or 2 and above is worse
strat.corn-to-premium.p.3.name: buildThreshold
strat.corn-to-premium.p.3.meaning: In the build phase a building's “value” must reach this number before it is bought (it also affects whether Builder is chosen). Too low buys a pile of useless buildings, too high buys almost nothing; every style is sensitive to it.
strat.corn-to-premium.p.3.range: 3–4 is better; 6 and above is worse
strat.harbor-rush.title: Harbor rush
strat.harbor-rush.summary: First works out how to build the Harbor (+1 point per shipment), then scores by shipping many times and many kinds of goods.
strat.harbor-rush.rule.0: Buys nothing except the Harbor until it is built; sells goods, collects role coins and uses quarry / builder-privilege discounts to raise money, and chooses Builder the moment there is enough.
strat.harbor-rush.rule.1: Once the Harbor is built it wants “many separate shipments”: several goods (corn / indigo / sugar), the Wharf, and choosing Captain as often as possible.
strat.harbor-rush.rule.2: When two plantation choices score exactly the same, a fixed order applies: Hacienda > corn > sugar > indigo > tobacco > coffee > quarry (sugar before indigo is better; override with the text parameter tieTile, an empty string turns it off).
strat.harbor-rush.rule.3: 4 players: first accumulates harborReadyTiles plantations (or reaches round harborReadyRound) before going for the Harbor, playing the normal economy until then; with 3 players it goes for it from the start (waiting is worse with 3 players).
strat.harbor-rush.p.0.name: quarryTarget
strat.harbor-rush.p.0.meaning: How many quarries to take before building the Harbor (quarries make buildings cheaper).
strat.harbor-rush.p.1.name: harborReadyTiles
strat.harbor-rush.p.1.meaning: 4 players: how many plantations/quarries to own before going for the Harbor; 0 = from the start.
strat.harbor-rush.p.1.range: 6–8 is better; 9 and above is worse
strat.harbor-rush.p.2.name: harborReadyRound
strat.harbor-rush.p.2.meaning: From which round to go for the Harbor regardless.
strat.harbor-rush.p.3.name: buildThreshold
strat.harbor-rush.p.3.meaning: In the build phase a building's “value” must reach this number before it is bought (it also affects whether Builder is chosen). Too low buys a pile of useless buildings, too high buys almost nothing; every style is sensitive to it.
strat.build-first.title: Build first
strat.build-first.summary: Turns coins into buildings as fast as possible, aiming for large buildings whose end-game bonus can be fully earned.
strat.build-first.rule.0: Takes quarries (building discount), grows mixed crops (indigo, sugar, tobacco, coffee) and sells goods for coins.
strat.build-first.rule.1: Chooses Builder whenever there is a building worth buying and affordable.
strat.build-first.rule.2: Picks large buildings by “can the bonus be fully earned”: Residence (many plantations), City Hall (many purple buildings), Guild Hall (many production buildings), Fortress (many colonists), Customs House (many victory-point chips).
strat.build-first.rule.4: When two plantation choices score exactly the same, a fixed order applies: Hacienda > corn > sugar > indigo > tobacco > coffee > quarry (sugar before indigo is better; override with the text parameter tieTile, an empty string turns it off).
strat.build-first.p.0.name: buildThreshold
strat.build-first.p.0.meaning: In the build phase a building's “value” must reach this number before it is bought (it also affects whether Builder is chosen). Too low buys a pile of useless buildings, too high buys almost nothing; every style is sensitive to it.
strat.build-first.p.0.range: 4 players: 4.5 is best (3.5 and below is much worse); 3 players: 3.5
strat.build-first.p.1.name: quarryTarget
strat.cheap-engine.title: Cheap engine
strat.cheap-engine.summary: Distilled from how MCTS plays: buys cheap 1-point buildings very early, grows very few plantations and ships small amounts often.
strat.cheap-engine.rule.0: Early on buys cheap 1-point buildings: Small Indigo Plant, Small Sugar Mill, Small Market, plus Hospice; later the Large Indigo Plant and Large Sugar Mill.
strat.cheap-engine.rule.1: Takes only corn / indigo / sugar plantations, and few of them: stops choosing Settler once it owns tileCap tiles.
strat.cheap-engine.rule.2: Does not buy the Hacienda; quarries are valued low.
strat.cheap-engine.rule.3: Chooses Captain whenever it holds goods (many shipments, small amounts); Trader is valued higher with a Small Market.
strat.cheap-engine.p.0.name: buildThreshold
strat.cheap-engine.p.0.meaning: In the build phase a building's “value” must reach this number before it is bought (it also affects whether Builder is chosen). Too low buys a pile of useless buildings, too high buys almost nothing; every style is sensitive to it.
strat.cheap-engine.p.0.range: 1–2 is best; 3 and above is worse
strat.cheap-engine.p.1.name: tileCap
strat.cheap-engine.p.1.meaning: After owning this many plantations it stops choosing the Settler role (it still gets plantations when others choose Settler).
strat.cheap-engine.p.1.range: 3–4 is best; 8 and above is much worse
strat.cheap-engine.p.2.name: smallValue
strat.cheap-engine.p.2.meaning: Value of the cheap 1-point buildings (Small Indigo Plant, Small Sugar Mill, Small Market).
strat.cheap-engine.p.2.range: 8 and above are all the same; 6 and below is worse
strat.cheap-engine.p.3.name: roleCoinWeight
strat.cheap-engine.p.3.meaning: When choosing a role, how many points each coin on the role card (and the Prospector's 1 coin) is worth.
strat.cheap-engine.p.3.range: 4 players 2 and 3 players 2.5 are clearly better (sweep round 13, analysis section 9); 4 and above gets worse
strat.wharf-rush.title: Wharf rush
strat.wharf-rush.summary: Farms for a while, raises the money (quarry discount) to buy the Wharf, then every Captain phase throws the biggest pile of goods onto the private ship.
strat.wharf-rush.rule.0: Early (fewer than wharfReadyTiles plantations and before round wharfReadyRound): mostly corn plus indigo / sugar, the default economy, no hurry to buy the Wharf.
strat.wharf-rush.rule.1: After the start: buys nothing but the Wharf; takes quarryTarget quarries (each discounts 1 coin, at most 3), sells indigo / sugar etc. for coins, and chooses Builder as soon as it has 9 coins.
strat.wharf-rush.rule.2: Once the Wharf is bought: staffs the Wharf first, then buys warehouses (so the big pile survives the Captain phase) and the Harbor (+1 point per shipment); the Harbor is optional.
strat.wharf-rush.rule.3: Shipping: the private ship always takes the biggest pile first (ignoring capacity and the public ships; the whole pile scores), the other goods go on public ships; warehouses keep the biggest pile; chooses Captain more often when holding a big pile.
strat.wharf-rush.rule.4: Corn is not sold (it is the main thing the private ship ships).
strat.wharf-rush.rule.5: When two plantation choices score exactly the same, a fixed order applies: Hacienda > corn > sugar > indigo > tobacco > coffee > quarry (corn must come before quarry; sugar before indigo is better; override with the text parameter tieTile, an empty string turns it off).
strat.wharf-rush.p.0.name: quarryTarget
strat.wharf-rush.p.0.meaning: The most quarries to take after the start (the Wharf's discount cap is 3 coins).
strat.wharf-rush.p.0.range: 3 and above are all the same; 0 is much worse
strat.wharf-rush.p.1.name: wharfReadyTiles
strat.wharf-rush.p.1.meaning: How many plantations/quarries before it starts buying the Wharf.
strat.wharf-rush.p.1.range: 7 and above are similar; 3–5 is worse
strat.wharf-rush.p.2.name: wharfReadyRound
strat.wharf-rush.p.2.meaning: From which round it starts buying the Wharf (whichever of this and the previous comes first).
strat.wharf-rush.p.3.name: smallPlant
strat.wharf-rush.p.3.meaning: Before buying the Wharf, the value of the Small Indigo Plant / Small Sugar Mill (the source of money from selling goods).
strat.wharf-rush.p.3.range: 3 players: 8 is better (+1.5 percentage points); no difference with 4 players
strat.wharf-rush.p.4.name: traderWeight
strat.wharf-rush.p.4.meaning: Value multiplier of the Trader role while saving for the Wharf.
strat.wharf-rush.p.5.name: moneyTile
strat.wharf-rush.p.5.meaning: Value of indigo / sugar plantations (+1 after the start).
strat.wharf-rush.p.6.name: cornTile
strat.wharf-rush.p.7.name: earlyQuarry
strat.wharf-rush.p.7.meaning: Value of quarries before the start.
strat.wharf-rush.p.7.range: 6; grabbing quarries early (9 and above) does not help
strat.wharf-rush.p.8.name: buildThreshold
strat.wharf-rush.p.8.meaning: In the build phase a building's “value” must reach this number before it is bought (it also affects whether Builder is chosen). Too low buys a pile of useless buildings, too high buys almost nothing; every style is sensitive to it.
strat.wharf-premium.title: Wharf rush (tobacco/coffee fundraising)
strat.wharf-premium.summary: A variant of the Wharf rush: first sets up tobacco or coffee production, sells to the trading house to raise the 9 coins for the Wharf, then throws the biggest pile onto the private ship as usual.
strat.wharf-premium.rule.0: Phase 1: picks the easier of tobacco and coffee, takes its plantations (and corn too) and first buys the matching production building (Tobacco Storage / Coffee Roaster).
strat.wharf-premium.rule.1: Phase 2 (has the production building, no Wharf yet): buys nothing but the Wharf; always sells tobacco / coffee for coins, Trader value is multiplied by traderWeight; takes at most quarryTarget quarries.
strat.wharf-premium.rule.2: Phase 3 (has the Wharf): the private ship takes the biggest pile first, the rest go on public ships; buys warehouses and the Harbor; with sellAfterWharf=1 goods worth 3 coins or more are still sold.
strat.wharf-premium.rule.3: Before buying the Wharf, choosing Captain only counts how much corn can be shipped (tobacco / coffee are kept to sell).
strat.wharf-premium.p.0.name: traderWeight
strat.wharf-premium.p.0.meaning: Value multiplier of the Trader role before the Wharf is bought.
strat.wharf-premium.p.1.name: quarryTarget
strat.wharf-premium.p.2.name: sellAfterWharf
strat.wharf-premium.p.2.meaning: Whether to keep selling premium goods after buying the Wharf (1 = sell, 0 = keep everything to ship).
strat.wharf-premium.p.3.name: cornTile
strat.wharf-premium.p.3.meaning: Value of corn plantations (plantations of the target good are 9.5).
strat.wharf-premium.p.4.name: buildThreshold
strat.wharf-premium.p.4.meaning: In the build phase a building's “value” must reach this number before it is bought (it also affects whether Builder is chosen). Too low buys a pile of useless buildings, too high buys almost nothing; every style is sensitive to it.
strat.corn-monopoly.title: Corn monopoly (disruptive)
strat.corn-monopoly.summary: A spoiler who just wants to take part: hogs every corn plantation, hoards corn without selling or shipping it, and uses up the limited corn supply.
strat.corn-monopoly.rule.0: Takes only corn plantations (even the face-up ones); choosing Settler is valued highest when corn is available.
strat.corn-monopoly.rule.1: Corn goods are neither sold nor shipped voluntarily; the Captain role is worth 0, and when forced to ship it ships other goods first and corn last.
strat.corn-monopoly.rule.2: Buys only warehouses (to keep the corn through the Captain phase), Hacienda and Hospice; no other buildings.
strat.corn-monopoly.rule.3: Staffs corn plantations and warehouses; values corn output when choosing Craftsman (the supply has only 10 corn, so once hoarded nobody else has any).
strat.corn-monopoly.p.0.name: buildThreshold
strat.corn-monopoly.p.0.meaning: In the build phase a building's “value” must reach this number before it is bought (it also affects whether Builder is chosen). Too low buys a pile of useless buildings, too high buys almost nothing; every style is sensitive to it.
strat.corn-monopoly-tiles.title: Corn monopoly: plantations only
strat.corn-monopoly-tiles.summary: A variant of the monopoly that separates the two disruptive tactics: only hogs corn plantations, goods are shipped and sold as usual.
strat.corn-monopoly-tiles.rule.0: Takes only corn plantations (even face-up ones) and rushes to choose Settler when corn is available.
strat.corn-monopoly-tiles.rule.1: Everything else is the same as the corn shipper: ships and buys buildings as usual.
strat.corn-monopoly-tiles.p.0.name: buildThreshold
strat.corn-monopoly-tiles.p.0.meaning: In the build phase a building's “value” must reach this number before it is bought (it also affects whether Builder is chosen). Too low buys a pile of useless buildings, too high buys almost nothing; every style is sensitive to it.
strat.corn-monopoly-hoard.title: Corn monopoly: hoarding only
strat.corn-monopoly-hoard.summary: A variant of the monopoly that separates the two disruptive tactics: takes plantations the way the corn shipper does, but hoards corn without selling or shipping it.
strat.corn-monopoly-hoard.rule.0: Plantation choices are the same as the corn shipper (no special grabbing).
strat.corn-monopoly-hoard.rule.1: Corn is neither sold nor shipped voluntarily; Captain is worth 0 and when forced to ship it ships other goods first; buys only warehouses, Hacienda and Hospice.
strat.corn-monopoly-hoard.p.0.name: buildThreshold
strat.corn-monopoly-hoard.p.0.meaning: In the build phase a building's “value” must reach this number before it is bought (it also affects whether Builder is chosen). Too low buys a pile of useless buildings, too high buys almost nothing; every style is sensitive to it.
strat.mcts.title: MCTS tree search
strat.mcts.summary: Finds the best action for every decision with many random simulations; the strongest but very slow, suited to a few hundred games.
strat.mcts.rule.0: Every decision: copies the current state, reshuffles the hidden plantation deck and runs simulations simulations.
strat.mcts.rule.1: Each simulation: walks down the search tree (UCT) → expands an untried action → rolloutStrategy plays all seats for rolloutRounds rounds → returns the score ranking at that point.
strat.mcts.rule.2: Finally picks the most-visited action. It sees the full state (including opponents' victory-point chips) but does not peek at the decks.
strat.mcts.rule.3: The amount of computation is limited by the number of simulations only (never by time), so the same config and seed reproduce exactly.
strat.mcts.p.0.name: simulations
strat.mcts.p.0.meaning: Simulations per decision; more is stronger and slower (roughly proportional).
strat.mcts.p.0.range: 100 simulations roughly match the hand-written strategies, 300 win by a wide margin
strat.mcts.p.1.name: exploration
strat.mcts.p.1.meaning: UCT exploration coefficient (rewards lie between 0 and 1).
strat.mcts.p.2.name: rolloutRounds
strat.mcts.p.2.meaning: How many rounds a simulation plays before stopping and ranking by the score at that point; 0 = play to the end.
strat.mcts.p.2.range: 5–8; 3 is too short; 8 is as strong as playing to the end but twice as fast
strat.mcts.p.3.name: rolloutStrategy
strat.mcts.p.3.meaning: The strategy all seats use in simulations; it cannot be mcts. Random is the most accurate; hand-written strategies and guided-random are worse.
strat.mcts.p.4.name: rolloutMaxDecisions
strat.mcts.p.4.meaning: The most decisions in one simulation (safety cap).
strat.mcts.p.5.name: valueModel
strat.mcts.p.5.meaning: A learned position-value function (a LightGBM text model .txt or an MLP .json, see ml/README.md). Once set, leaf nodes no longer roll out to round rolloutRounds; the model estimates each seat's return instead and rolloutRounds is ignored.
strat.mcts.p.5.range: Use the model matching the player count
strat.mcts.p.6.name: leafRollout
strat.mcts.p.6.meaning: With a valueModel, how many decisions rolloutStrategy plays after expansion before evaluating; 0 = evaluate directly.
strat.random.title: Random actions
strat.random.summary: Picks uniformly at random among the legal actions every time, as the weakest baseline.
strat.random.rule.0: No strategy at all; used to confirm the other strategies really beat random play.
strat.guided-random.title: Weighted random
strat.guided-random.summary: Random, but weighted by action type: rarely passes, prefers shipping, building, selling and taking plantations.
strat.guided-random.rule.0: In experiments, as MCTS's simulation strategy it did worse than pure random (a biased simulation evaluates less accurately).
strat.group.corn.title: 🌽 Corn
strat.group.corn.hint: The main good is corn: ship it, switch to premium goods, or hog corn to disrupt.
strat.group.ship.title: ⚓ Harbor / private ship
strat.group.ship.hint: Scores through the shipping bonus of the Harbor or the Wharf.
strat.group.build.title: 🏗️ Buildings
strat.group.build.hint: Turns coins into buildings: the end-game bonus of large buildings, or cheap 1-point buildings.
strat.group.search.title: 🎲 Search / random
strat.group.search.hint: Not hand-written rules: tree search and the random players used as baselines.
sim.title: Simulate
sim.intro: Pick the player count and a strategy for every seat, then press “Start simulation”. The result is saved in the results folder, loaded automatically when done, and can be viewed on the “Results” page.
sim.template_label: Use a result file's settings as a template
sim.template_note: Reads only the settings, not the whole result, so big files are fast too. You can also press “Simulate again with these settings” on the Results page.
sim.balanced_error: Fully balanced needs a number of games that is a multiple of {0} ({1} have {0} seat permutations and each must be used equally often); you have {2} games, so the last {3} would leave the permutations slightly unbalanced.
sim.mcts_warn: {0} seat(s) use MCTS, {1} games in total: this will take a long time (roughly {2}, estimated for this machine's {3} cores). MCTS is hundreds of times slower than the hand-written strategies; start with a few hundred games or lower the simulations parameter.
sim.model_title: A learned position-value model (trained in the ML UI, kept in ml/models/): leaf nodes use the model's estimate instead of rolling out. It is written into the parameter box on the left (valueModel=…).
sim.note_params: Every strategy's behaviour rules and tunable parameters are under “Strategy guide” at the bottom of the page. Parameter box format: name=value (a number, or text such as rolloutStrategy=random), several separated by commas, for example buildThreshold=3.5, quarryTarget=2.
sim.sweep_label: Sweep parameters (target seat): one parameter per line, name=value,value,…; the grid is every combination of the parameters
sim.sweep_note: Every grid point uses the same main seed and the same opponents and changes only the target seat's parameters, so points are directly comparable; the seat's fixed parameters are overridden by the sweep values. Parameters that can be swept: buildThreshold (all hand-written strategies), quarryTarget (build-first, harbor-rush), switchRound / cornTarget (corn-to-premium).
sim.sweep_done: Sweep finished, saved to {0} ({1}, {2} grid points).
sim.guide_note: Defaults written as “4p / 3p” mean the strategy picks different defaults by player count automatically; a value you type explicitly in a seat's parameter box always wins. “Suggested range” comes from the parameter-sweep experiments (see docs/strategy-analysis.md).
sim.ties:
All hand-written strategies also have an experimental parameter randomTies (default 0): when scores are exactly equal, 0 = pick the first action in engine order, 1 = random when the Settler and Craftsman extra goods tie, 2 = random on ties in every phase except Mayor (3 = Settler only, 4 = Craftsman extra good only). It changes win rates, see docs/strategy-analysis.md 8.1.
Fixed orders for ties (none is set by default, which keeps engine order): tieTile (taking a plantation: corn indigo sugar tobacco coffee quarry hacienda), tieGood (Craftsman extra good, selling, shipping, keeping: the five goods), tieRole (choosing a role), tieBuild (buildings, including pass), written as a text parameter such as tieTile=sugar>indigo>coffee, highest priority first, unlisted ones last; it only matters when scores are exactly equal and never overrides a real score difference. Reserved: tieOpponent (a weight, default 0), which on ties prefers (positive) or avoids (negative) the good the opponents currently produce the most barrels of. See 8.2.

fp.label: Result file

res.intro: Load the result.json written by the Runner (--out) to inspect strategy win rates, scores and endings. A strategy's colour is fixed to the strategy and does not change with rank.
res.again_title: Takes this result's player count, strategies, parameters and seed to the Simulate page, where you can edit them and run again
res.sweep_loaded: A parameter-sweep result is loaded; view it on the “Parameter Sweep” page.
res.copy_note: Copies the settings, win rates, duration and versions (no per-game data, no local paths) to paste into a conversation with an AI.
res.status_warn: This result's status is “{0}”; it contains only the {1} games finished out of {2} planned.
res.winrate_note: Win rate = share of games won (ties for first share the win); error bar = 95% confidence interval. Random baseline = {0}.
res.score_note: Bar = average total score; line = ±1 standard deviation (how spread out the scores are; shorter is steadier).
res.parts_note: Per game on average: shipping chips / building points / large-building bonus; sorted by total score, highest first.
res.seat_note: Win rate of each table position (seat 1 = starting governor). The strategies' seats were rotated, so this shows only the advantage of the position itself.
res.behaviour_note: Per-game averages. Harbor rate = share of the strategy's games in which the Harbor was built, round = the average round it was built; shipments include the Wharf.
res.buildings_note: Win rate of the players who own the building (all strategies combined), baseline = {0}. Buildings with fewer than 300 owners are not drawn (too few samples) and only those above 25% are listed; the full data is in the table below.
res.buildings_chart: Win rate of players who own the building
res.buildings_tip: {0}  {1} owners, win rate {2} (without it {3}), bought on average in round {4}
res.all_buildings: All buildings (ownership rate, purchase round, win rate)
res.old_file: This result file was written by an older version and has no building list or behaviour statistics; run it again with a newer Runner to get “Strategy behaviour” and “Buildings and win rate”.
res.pairwise_note: The probability that the row strategy ranks higher than the column strategy (games with equal ranks excluded). Blue = row stronger, red = column stronger, grey = evenly matched.
res.no_records: This result has no per-game records (output.perGameRecords: false), so there is no game length, end reason or rank comparison.
res.games_note: Browse and filter game by game (the data comes from the result file's per-game records); “Replay” plays that game again so you can see every step's board and action explanation.
gl.player_legend: One player matching all of these (the same player must satisfy every condition)
gl.no_building_records: This result file has no building or end-of-game plantation records, so buildings and plantations cannot be filtered.
ov.intro: Tick several normal simulation result files (for example the 4-player full table and the four 3-player combinations produced from tournaments/); every strategy is summarised by player count: its win rate is averaged over the tables (every table has the same weight) and the win rate of each table is listed. “Edge” = average win rate − the equal-share baseline (1/players).
ov.preset_none: none yet, tick files and save first
ov.empty_folder: There are no usable result files in the folder
ov.note: Scanned folder: {0}. Click a whole row or its checkbox to select; the header checkbox selects / clears every listed file (narrow the list with the filter above first). Parameter-sweep files (sweep) and files that cannot be read are not listed; every large file takes a few seconds to load.
ov.biased: Some tables in this group use the Rotate or Fixed seat order: a table that uses a single cyclic arrangement can be off by 20 percentage points or more, so it cannot be compared directly with the other tables. Run it again with Random or Balanced.
ov.mixed: The tables in this group use different seat orders; keep that in mind when averaging win rates.
ov.tip: {0}  average win rate {1} ± {2} ({3} tables, range {4} – {5}), equal-share baseline {6}
ov.matrix_note: Each cell = the share of games in which the row strategy ranked above the column strategy (ties not counted), averaged over all tables where the two sat together; the result files need per-game records. A darker colour means the row has more of the advantage.
cmp.intro: Pick two normal simulation result files and compare win rates and average scores by strategy name. A is the baseline and B is the new one; difference = B − A. A difference is marked “significant” only when it exceeds its 95% confidence interval (the two are assumed to be independent samples; with the same main seed the difference is actually steadier, so this judgement is conservative).
cmp.warn: The two files have different {0}; the difference may come from the table rather than the strategy itself.

rp.board_note: Shows the board before decision {0} (the player to move has a blue frame); drag to the far right for the final board; the keyboard ← / → switches to the previous / next step. A ● in a tile means a colonist, and ●○ under a building name are colonists / empty slots.

rp.row_title: Click to see the position before this step on the board above

ms.title: MCTS search
ms.rollout_title: After the tree search, all seats (opponents and itself) play on with this strategy up to the stopping point; it decides how the opponents play in the simulations.
ms.model_title: Leaf nodes are not played to the stopping point; a learned position-value model estimates every seat's outcome instead (the win-rate column is then also the model's estimate).
ms.rounds_title: After this many rounds the score ranking at that point is taken as the result; playing to the end is the most accurate but slowest.
ms.explore_title: UCT exploration coefficient: the larger it is, the more willing it is to try unpopular actions.
ms.legend: Chosen action (average reward compared with the 2nd most simulated):
ms.dq_title: Chosen action's Q − this row's Q
ms.noise_title: The threshold the Q difference must exceed when the chosen action is compared with this row
ms.next_unvisited: The next simulation will pick this one (largest UCT); there are also actions not simulated yet, which the search tries first
ms.next: The next simulation will pick this one (largest UCT)
la.none_title: This seat's strategy has no search (or this step had no choice), so there are no scores; it only lists every legal action at that moment.
la.sorted_title: The hand-written strategy scores every legal action and the highest score is chosen (ties go to the one listed first).
la.forced: Only one legal action, played automatically
la.forced_title: With only one legal action the engine plays it directly without asking the strategy.
la.mayor: Mayor phase: colonists are placed one at a time and positions may only go from small to large (so the same distribution is not repeated), so this lists “where the next colonist goes”, not the whole distribution.
la.score: Score is a heuristic score defined by the strategy itself; it has no 0–1 meaning, cannot be compared with MCTS's Q, can be negative, and only the relative order matters.
la.score_mayor: In the Mayor phase the Score is “the value of this position”; the best set of positions is picked first and then placed in turn, so the chosen one is not necessarily the highest score.
la.tie_title: The strategy's fixed order when scores are equal (1 = highest priority)
la.opp_title: Second key when scores are equal: barrels the opponents currently produce × the tieOpponent weight
ms.help.1: Visit count N (Visits): how many times simulations passed through this node; the larger N is, the more reliable the conclusion; when the iterations finish, the child of the root with the largest N is chosen as the final action
ms.help.3: Average reward Q: the mean of r over all simulations passing through this node, between 0 and 1; for “the decision player of that node”, a larger Q means a better average outcome
ms.help.4: Standard error SE: the uncertainty of the average reward Q, SE = σ ÷ √N; the smaller SE is, the steadier and more reliable Q is (the larger N, the smaller SE)
ms.help.5: Difference ΔQ: the chosen action's Q minus that row's Q (not shown for the chosen row); a ΔQ above Noise is green (the chosen one is clearly better), below −Noise is red (that row is clearly better), otherwise no colour
ms.help.6: Noise: the threshold the Q difference between the chosen action and that row must exceed; Noise = {0} × √(SE_chosen² + SE_row²); if the Q difference does not exceed Noise it may just be luck (not shown for the chosen row)
ms.help.7: UCT: Q + C × √(ln N_parent ÷ N_child); selection walks down the child with the highest UCT; the exploration bonus lets rarely tried actions get picked
ms.help.8: Signal (chosen row vs 2nd, noise = {0} × the combined standard error): green: clearly not luck; yellow: slightly ahead, with noise or too few samples; red: too few simulations or low reward.

sw.intro: Load the sweep.json written by Runner --sweep. Every grid point uses the same main seed and the same opponents and changes only the target strategy's parameters, so points can be compared directly.
sw.again_title: Takes this sweep's strategies, opponents and sweep parameters to the Simulate page

sw.points_note: Highest first; error bar = 95% confidence interval. Grid points whose confidence intervals overlap do not differ significantly.
sw.first40: Only the first 40 grid points are drawn; the full data is in the table below.
sw.heat_note: Rows = {0}, columns = {1}; a darker colour means a higher win rate.

vs.page_title: Version Control · Puerto Rico Strategy Simulator
vs.intro: All the version numbers (rules, engine, strategies…) and what each version changed. The source is docs/versions.json (the same file as the ML UI; its texts are written in Chinese).
vs.dirty: There were uncommitted changes at build time (-dirty)
vs.note: The rules version covers only the game rules and randomness, and every strategy has its own strategy version; these two version numbers together with the full parameters decide the ML tools' hash, which tells whether data and models are out of date. The engine version is for people and the commit is only for tracing (not in the hash); an engineCommit with “-dirty” in a result file means there were uncommitted changes at the time.
